### PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values
- Canonical URL: https://ainewsradar.xyz/news/d345f3b9dd8d65d8
- Primary Source: THE DECODER (https://the-decoder.com/prismml-squeezes-an-agent-based-coding-model-with-27-billion-parameters-into-5-9-gb/)
- Executive Summary: Startup PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an updated version of its aggressively compressed language model. It's based on Qwen3.8-27B and takes up just 5.9 GB of memory, same as its predecessor. That's possible because of ternary quantization, where each weight can only be one of three values (−1, 0, or +1) instead of the usual 16-bit storage. At full precision, a model this size would need about 54 GB. Bonsai 2.5 is designed to perform more reliably on agentic tasks that involve lon
- Key Verified Facts:

### MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
- Canonical URL: https://ainewsradar.xyz/news/9621f902080b1b57

- Executive Summary: Researchers from MIT, ETH Zurich, and Imperial College London have developed a method to train AI climate emulators using synthetic data characterized by extreme environmental fluctuations, such as sudden CO2 spikes. This approach allows models to achieve high precision and robustness with only a single simulation run, significantly reducing computational demand.
- Key Verified Facts:

* [Root Cause & Mechanism] To address the computational intensity and generalization limitations of traditional physics-based climate simulations
* [Key Fact Detail] Incorporating extreme-fluctuation synthetic data into AI training.
* [Key Position & Outlook] Enhanced model robustness for non-standard climate scenario prediction.
